forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.paper_title: Budget and Treasury Monitoring - Quarter 2 2026/2027 (1st April 2026 to 30th September 2026)
findings.headline: MUFG forecasts Bank Rate rising to 4% in Q4 2026, and investment earnings are forecast at 4.0% for H2 2026/27
findings.detail: MUFG's forecast of 21 September 2026 expects a rise most likely on 5 November, with Bank Rate projected to fall in H2 2027. The firm advises authorities to review their 2026/27 and 2027/28 investment income budgets, and says PWLB rates remain materially above its estimate of the longer-term neutral Bank Rate of 3.5%.
findings.matters: The rate path and the advice to review investment income budgets are the input that finance directors at other councils are using to set their own treasury assumptions.

findings.paper_title: Budget and Treasury Monitoring - Quarter 2 2026/2027 (1st April 2026 to 30th September 2026)
findings.headline: UKSPF/REPF programme has closed, with all programme areas meeting or exceeding forecast outputs
findings.detail: The paper states that all 2025/26 (2026/27) UKSPF/REPF programme allocations were spent in advance of the 30 September 2026 programme closure date, and the remaining local match is committed and will be spent by Q1 2027. Most outcomes are reported as met, with some to be realised over the next 12 months.
findings.matters: A grant programme that closed on time with outputs met is an outcome other councils managing the same closing programme will want to compare against.
findings.quote: All programme areas have met or exceeded forecast outputs

findings.paper_title: Budget and Treasury Monitoring - Quarter 2 2026/2027 (1st April 2026 to 30th September 2026)
findings.headline: Direct cremations were 24% of demand in the first six months, against a forecast of 20%, and a £0.017m income shortfall is forecast
findings.detail: Standard cremations were 67% of demand against a forecast of 71%. The paper attributes the shift to increased demand for direct cremations and farewell services, and says the next Business Plan covering 2028-2031 will be presented to the committee later in the financial year.
findings.matters: A change in the mix of service demand that shifts income away from the forecast is a service-level risk that other councils running crematoria will want to track.
findings.figures: 24% direct cremations of demand (forecast 20%); 67% standard cremations (forecast 71%); £0.017m forecast income shortfall

findings.paper_title: Budget and Treasury Monitoring - Quarter 2 2026/2027 (1st April 2026 to 30th September 2026)
findings.headline: Sundry debt over 90 days stands at £420,325 at the end of Quarter 2, against £205,618 at the end of Quarter 1
findings.detail: The paper says 97% of the debt over 90 days is over 150 days old. The largest elements are Development Control at £0.161m and Property Services at £0.123m, and recovery is under way on all debt over 90 days, with payment plans being put in place where possible.
findings.matters: A rise in aged sundry debt that is mostly over 150 days old is a recovery problem that finance officers at other councils will want to benchmark against.
